Build PHASE 1 of "Adloop" — a cross-platform paid-ads management SaaS — as an add-on module inside the Nxeon platform (Next.js App Router + Prisma + Postgres at /opt/nxeon). Placeholder brand: name "Adloop", palette emerald #10B981 + amber #F59E0B + slate-900 #0F172A, tagline "Your ads, on autopilot.", placeholder domain ads.revsports.ca (store as config).

READ FIRST:
- /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/ads/architecture.md
- /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/ads/board.json (implement the "Phase 1" column).
Study Nxeon conventions: lib/admin-groups.ts (ADMIN_NAV — add a new top-level section), lib/rbac.ts (HREF_AREA + requireArea → area "platform"), components/ui/primitives.tsx (reuse primitives), an existing admin page + lib/actions-*.ts, components/portal/Shell.tsx icons map (use existing key like "chart" or "bolt").

=== HARD GUARDRAILS ===
- Branch `feature/ads-adloop-phase1` off main (main is at 5a053b9). Commit + `git push -u origin feature/ads-adloop-phase1`. Do NOT commit to main, do NOT deploy, do NOT `prisma db push` any DB, do NOT edit .env.
- NO live calls to Meta / TikTok / Google Ads APIs. NO real OAuth to those platforms. NO ad spend. Connectors are SCAFFOLDING/STUBS this phase — real API access is gated on weeks-long approvals (flag this in docs).
- `npx prisma generate` + `npm run build` MUST pass 0 errors; add tests where sensible.

=== PHASE 1 DELIVERABLES ===
1) Prisma schema (additive, prefix models `Ads*` to avoid collisions): AdsAccount (platform enum META/TIKTOK/GOOGLE, externalId, name, status enum DISCONNECTED/CONNECTED_STUB, connectedAt?), AdsCampaign (accountId, platform, name, objective, status, dailyBudgetCents, externalId?), AdsAdSet (campaignId, name, targetingJson, budgetCents), AdsCreative (adSetId, name, headline, body, imageRef?, status), AdsAd (adSetId, creativeId, name, status), AdsInsight (campaignId/adSetId/adId scope, date, impressions, clicks, spendCents, conversions — for stub/sample data), AdsRule (accountId, name, whenJson (metric/operator/threshold), thenJson (action e.g. pause/raise-budget), enabled) for the automation-rule skeleton, AdsRuleRun (ruleId, ranAt, matched bool, note). Sensible enums + indexes.
2) A unified data layer (lib/ads/*) that normalizes the three platforms behind one interface, with a PLUGGABLE connector seam (MetaConnector/TikTokConnector/GoogleConnector) whose methods are stubs returning typed "not connected / pending API approval" results — NO network calls. Include a rules-engine evaluator (pure, testable): given a rule's whenJson + an insight snapshot, decide if it matches and what action it would take (DRY-RUN only — never executes a real platform mutation this phase).
3) Admin UI under a NEW top-level nav section "Ads" (Adloop):
   - /admin/ads — Overview dashboard: connected accounts, campaigns, a unified stats panel (from AdsInsight sample/stub data), and a clear banner "Live ad-platform sync pending API approval (Meta/TikTok/Google)".
   - /admin/ads/accounts — list + "Connect" buttons that are STUBS (mark CONNECTED_STUB, explain the real OAuth/approval flow needed; no network).
   - /admin/ads/campaigns — browse campaigns/adsets/ads/creatives (CRUD as local drafts).
   - /admin/ads/rules — create automation rules (when/then), toggle enabled, and a "Test rule (dry-run)" that evaluates against current/sample insights and shows what it WOULD do — never executes.
   Server actions in lib/actions-ads.ts (each re-checks requireArea("platform")). Match admin look; sentence case.
4) A seed (prisma/seed-ads.ts, manual run only) with a couple of sample accounts/campaigns/insights so the dashboard renders with data on staging.
5) Update docs/DOCUMENTATION.md with an "Adloop (Ads Autopilot) — Phase 1" section, prominently noting the external API-approval prerequisites + timelines from the architecture doc.

When done: prisma generate + npm run build clean; commit + push the branch; report files added/changed, models added, build/test result, and the staging command `cd /opt/nxeon && bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh feature/ads-adloop-phase1`. Do not deploy.

1	# Ads Autopilot — Architecture & Product Plan
2	
3	_Research + planning document. Prepared 2026-08-10. No code, no external API calls, no deployment — planning only._
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Product Overview
8	
9	**Ads Autopilot** is a SaaS that connects a company's paid-ad accounts across **Meta (Facebook/Instagram), TikTok, and Google Ads**, then runs and optimizes campaigns from one control plane:
10	
11	- **Account connection** — OAuth into each platform, discover ad accounts, campaigns, ad sets/groups, ads.
12	- **Budget pacing** — keep spend on a target curve; prevent the classic 2x/day and 30.4x/month overspends.
13	- **Rules automation** — "if CPA > X for 3 days, pause"; scheduled dayparting; auto-scaling of winners.
14	- **Creative rotation / A-B testing** — rotate, promote winners, retire fatigued creatives.
15	- **AI creative generation** — reuse Nxeon's existing ad-creative tooling to generate images/copy variants.
16	- **Unified cross-platform reporting** — one schema, one dashboard, apples-to-apples across the three networks.
17	
18	It ships **two ways**: (a) a standalone Next.js app on the dev box (`51.79.226.215`), and (b) an add-on module inside the Nxeon admin portal (Nxeon is the central hub).
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 2. Competitors & Positioning
23	
24	| Tool | Focus | Pricing (2026) |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| **Madgicx** | Meta-only AI optimization + creative/audience insight | from ~$49/mo, ad-spend tiered |
27	| **Revealbot** | Granular rule-based automation across Meta, Google, TikTok | from ~$99/mo, ad-spend tiered |
28	| **AdEspresso** | SMB-friendly split-testing UX over Meta + Google | from ~$49/mo, per-account |
29	| **Smartly.io** | Enterprise cross-channel creative + campaign orchestration | unpublished; ~$5k/mo floor, ~$90k median annual |
30	| **Metadata.io** | B2B, revenue/pipeline-optimized, multi-channel (LinkedIn, Meta, Google, Bing, Reddit), AI agents | custom; reports of ~$60k |
31	
32	**Positioning gap Ads Autopilot targets:** Revealbot has the automation but is a bare rules engine; Madgicx is Meta-only; Smartly/Metadata are enterprise-priced. **Ads Autopilot = Revealbot-class cross-platform automation + built-in AI creative generation (via Nxeon), at SMB/agency pricing, bundled into the Nxeon hosting/marketing ecosystem** as a differentiator (existing Nxeon customers get ads managed where their site already lives).
33	
34	Sources: [Smartly vs Madgicx](https://admanage.ai/blog/smartly-vs-madgicx), [Meta ads automation pricing](https://adlibrary.com/guides/meta-ads-automation-software-pricing-9-options-compared), [Madgicx review](https://www.get-ryze.ai/blog/madgicx-review-2026-meta-ads-alternatives), [Metadata.io review](https://saleshive.com/vendors/metadata-io).
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 3. API Access Requirements & Approval Timelines — **THE LONG POLE**
39	
40	> **BIGGEST BLOCKER: API approvals gate the entire product.** Nothing beyond a self-account demo works until these clear. Meta advanced access + business verification and Google Ads Basic/Standard access are the critical path — **budget 4–8 weeks of calendar time, start Day 1, in parallel.** All three require a legal business entity, a verified business, a public privacy policy + working product demo/screencast, and a real client-onboarding flow (not just your own accounts).
41	
42	### 3.1 Meta Marketing API
43	- **Tiers:** Every new app starts on **Standard Access** (dev tier) — only your own/admin ad accounts, ~60-point rate quota. **Advanced Access** (standard tier) is required to manage *third-party* clients' ads and unlocks the ~9,000-point quota. (Note: on 2026-05-04 Meta renamed AMSA to "Marketing API Access Tier" with **Limited vs Full Access** levels.)
44	- **Requirements for Advanced/Full:** formal **App Review**, **Business Verification** (legal docs; mandatory for `ads_management` advanced access and for programmatic ad-account creation), a **screencast demonstrating each permission live**, a **working client-onboarding flow**, and a public privacy policy.
45	- **Permissions:** `ads_management`, `ads_read`, `business_management`, `pages_read_engagement`/`pages_manage_ads` as needed.
46	- **Timeline:** Business Verification a few business days; App Review commonly **1–3+ weeks**, longer if the reviewer bounces the screencast. Plan for iteration.
47	- **Rate limits:** Business-Use-Case (BUC) point system, separate pools for `ads_insights` vs `ads_management`; hard cap 100 POST/sec; heavy insight pulls with breakdowns cost more points. Design centralized pacing.
48	
49	Sources: [Meta app review guide](https://singhamandeep.com/facebook-ads-api-permission-app-review/), [Advanced access](https://singhamandeep.com/what-is-meta-advanced-access/), [Access levels for agencies](https://www.adamigo.ai/blog/meta-ads-api-access-levels-for-agencies), [Meta rate limiting docs](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/overview/rate-limiting/), [AdManage limits](https://admanage.ai/blog/meta-ads-api).
50	
51	### 3.2 Google Ads API
52	- **Developer token levels (per official docs):**
53	  - **Test Account** — test accounts only, 15,000 ops/day. Immediate.
54	  - **Explorer** — test + production, **2,880 ops/day** on production. Often auto-granted.
55	  - **Basic** — test + production, 15,000 ops/day. **~5 business-day review.**
56	  - **Standard** — unlimited for most services. **~10 business-day review**; for large/multi-user tools; needs demo + Required Minimum Functionality compliance.
57	- **Prerequisites:** token is tied to a **Manager (MCC) account**; **OAuth 2.0** per client; Google Cloud project. A **brand-verification pilot (launched 2026-07-07)** can cut a pending review from days to hours.
58	- **Timeline:** token approval typically **5–14 business days**; brand verification may shortcut. Start with test account immediately.
59	
60	Sources: [Access levels](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/access-levels), [Developer token](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/get-started/dev-token), [Basic access guide](https://www.slobodan-jelisavac.com/en/blog/google-ads-api-basic-access-guide).
61	
62	### 3.3 TikTok Marketing API
63	- **Access:** developer registration → app creation → **Business Center onboarding** → sandbox-to-production **app review** → business verification for higher volume → data-security compliance audit.
64	- **Capabilities:** campaign management, reporting, audience operations; v1.3 with OAuth. (Content Posting API is separate, needs audit; not core to ads mgmt.)
65	- **Timeline:** basic Marketing API **~3–7 business days** (faster for established business accounts with ad history); advanced/high-volume tiers **1–3 weeks**; quota increases are case-by-case with **no self-serve path and no published SLA**.
66	- **Rate limits:** 1-minute sliding window, ~600 RPM/endpoint baseline; per-app, per-token, per-advertiser quotas → needs **centralized request pacing**.
67	
68	Sources: [TikTok rate limits](https://www.getphyllo.com/post/tiktok-api-rate-limits-in-2026-quotas-errors-workarounds), [Marketing API v1.3](https://soku.ai/blog/tiktok-marketing-api-v1-3-explained), [Business API setup](https://tiktok.savvyshopperhubs.com/tiktok-business-api-guide/).
69	
70	### 3.4 API Capability Matrix (all three broadly support)
71	| Capability | Meta | Google Ads | TikTok |
72	|---|---|---|---|
73	| Campaign/AdSet(Group)/Ad CRUD | ✅ | ✅ (mutate ops) | ✅ |
74	| Budget get/set | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
75	| Creative upload (image/video) | ✅ | ✅ (assets) | ✅ |
76	| Insights/reporting | ✅ (BUC insights) | ✅ (GAQL) | ✅ |
77	| Audiences | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
78	| Recommendations | limited | ✅ (recommendations) | limited |
79	
80	Sources: [Google GAQL](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/query/overview), [Google mutate best practices](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/mutating/best-practices), [Opteo google-ads-api lib](https://github.com/Opteo/google-ads-api).
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 4. Recommended Tech Stack
85	
86	- **App:** Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript (matches Nxeon).
87	- **DB/ORM:** Postgres + Prisma.
88	- **Background jobs:** durable queue for pacing/rules ticks and insight syncs — BullMQ + Redis, or pg-boss (Postgres-native, one less dependency). Cron-style scheduler for periodic evaluation.
89	- **API clients:** official/community SDKs — `google-ads-api` (Opteo) for Google; typed fetch wrappers for Meta Graph and TikTok v1.3 (versioned).
90	- **Auth:** platform OAuth per client account; encrypted token vault (KMS or libsodium-sealed columns); auto-refresh worker.
91	- **Rate limiting:** centralized token-bucket per platform + per ad account, respecting BUC points (Meta), ops/day (Google), RPM windows (TikTok).
92	- **AI creative:** reuse **existing Nxeon ad-creative tooling** — do not rebuild.
93	- **Frontend:** React server components + a charting lib for reporting; shadcn/Tailwind to match Nxeon theme (brand cyan `#22D3EE`).
94	- **Observability:** structured logs + per-account API-quota dashboards; audit log of every mutation (compliance requirement).
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 5. Unified Data Model
99	
100	Normalize all three platforms into one schema (platform-specific fields in a `raw JSONB` column).
101	
102	```
103	Organization ─┐
104	              ├─< AdAccountConnection (platform enum, oauth tokens enc, external_account_id, status)
105	              │        └─< Campaign (external_id, objective, status, budget, budget_type)
106	              │              └─< AdSet   (a.k.a. AdGroup; targeting JSONB, budget, schedule)
107	              │                    └─< Ad (external_id, status, creative_id)
108	              ├─< Creative (type: image|video|carousel, asset_url, source: uploaded|ai_generated, nxeon_asset_ref)
109	              ├─< InsightSnapshot (entity_type, entity_id, date, impressions, clicks, spend, conversions, revenue, cpa, roas, ctr, cpm)  ← time-series
110	              ├─< Rule (name, scope, condition JSON, action JSON, schedule, enabled, last_run)
111	              ├─< RuleExecution (rule_id, entity_id, evaluated_at, matched, action_taken, result)
112	              ├─< BudgetPlan (entity_id, period, target_spend, pacing_strategy, cap)
113	              └─< AuditLog (actor, action, entity, before/after JSONB, platform_response)
114	```
115	
116	Key notes: `platform` enum {META, GOOGLE, TIKTOK}; keep a canonical metric set + `raw` JSONB for platform extras; store currency + timezone per account (pacing math depends on account TZ); `InsightSnapshot` is the reporting fact table (daily grain, backfilled + incrementally synced).
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 6. Automation / Rules Engine Design
121	
122	**Model:** each Rule = `{ scope (account/campaign/adset/ad, with filters), condition tree (AND/OR of metric comparisons over a lookback window), action, schedule, guardrails }`.
123	
124	- **Conditions:** metric (spend, CPA, ROAS, CTR, freq, conv) `op` threshold, over lookback (today / 3d / 7d), optional min-impressions floor to avoid acting on noise.
125	- **Actions:** pause/enable, adjust budget ±%/abs, adjust bid, rotate/pause creative, send alert (Nxeon notification/email), tag.
126	- **Scheduler:** evaluation ticks (e.g., every 15–60 min) pull latest insights → evaluate rules → enqueue mutations → write RuleExecution + AuditLog. Idempotent; dry-run mode.
127	- **Safety guardrails:** max budget-change per day, cooldown between actions on same entity, global kill-switch, require insights freshness before acting, never act below a statistical-significance floor.
128	- **Example:** "If campaign pacing ≥10% behind target on/after day 20 and ROAS ≥ target → raise daily budget +20%." (mirrors industry pattern).
129	
130	**Budget pacing logic:**
131	- Target curve = `target_period_spend × (elapsed_time_in_period / total_time)`, adjusted for dayparting weights.
132	- Each tick compute `pace_ratio = actual_spend / expected_spend`; if ahead → throttle daily budget / shift to standard delivery; if behind (and performance healthy) → raise budget toward cap.
133	- **Overspend guards:** respect platform realities — Google can spend up to **2x daily / 30.4x monthly**; enforce hard monthly cap by auto-pausing when projected month-end > cap. Daypart toward converting hours.
134	
135	Sources: [Google budget pacing formula](https://www.get-ryze.ai/blog/google-ads-daily-and-monthly-budget-pacing-rules), [FB budget pacing](https://wevion.ai/en/blog/budget-pacing-facebook-ads-guide/), [overspend prevention](https://ustechautomations.com/resources/blog/reduce-automated-campaign-budget-alerts-overspend-prevention-with-automation-2026).
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 7. Reporting
140	
141	- **Fact table:** `InsightSnapshot` (daily grain) synced incrementally; hourly for pacing-critical accounts.
142	- **Unified metrics:** spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, CPM, CPC, conversions, CPA, revenue, ROAS — normalized across platforms with a documented mapping (attribution windows differ per platform → label them).
143	- **Views:** cross-platform overview, per-platform drilldown, creative leaderboard, pacing/burn-down vs target, rule-activity feed, client-facing exportable reports (PDF/CSV).
144	- Cache aggregates; never hit live APIs on dashboard load (rate limits).
145	
146	---
147	
148	## 8. Standalone AND Nxeon Add-on
149	
150	**Shared core:** put all platform clients, data model, rules engine, pacing, and sync workers in a **framework-agnostic core package** (`@ads-autopilot/core`) that neither UI depends on directly.
151	
152	- **Standalone app:** own Next.js app + own Postgres on the dev box; own auth/billing; full multi-tenant SaaS.
153	- **Nxeon add-on:** mount as a module under `/admin/ads` in the Nxeon portal; reuse Nxeon auth, org model, notifications, billing, **and the AI ad-creative tooling**; the core package is imported and its workers run on Nxeon's job infra. Feature-flag it (`ENABLE_ADS_AUTOPILOT`) like other Nxeon modules until API access + security review pass.
154	- **Data:** either a shared schema namespaced (`ads_*` tables) inside Nxeon's DB, or a separate DB with the same Prisma schema — keep the migration reversible. Match Nxeon theme (cyan `#22D3EE`).
155	
156	---
157	
158	## 9. Phased Build Plan
159	
160	- **Phase 0 — Approvals & legal (Day 1, parallel, long-pole):** register apps, submit Meta business verification + app review, apply Google dev token (start on test), TikTok Business Center + app review. Draft privacy policy, ToS, data-handling doc. Build the demo/screencast flow reviewers require.
161	- **Phase 1 — Foundation + Meta read-only:** core package, data model, OAuth + token vault, Meta account/campaign/insight **sync (read)**, unified reporting dashboard, Nxeon `/admin/ads` shell. (Works under Standard access on own accounts.)
162	- **Phase 2 — Google + TikTok connectors:** add both platforms behind the same schema; unified cross-platform reporting.
163	- **Phase 3 — Write ops + rules engine:** mutations (pause/budget/bid), rules engine + scheduler, guardrails, audit log, dry-run.
164	- **Phase 4 — Budget pacing + creative:** pacing engine, dayparting, overspend guards; creative rotation/testing; AI creative generation via Nxeon tooling.
165	- **Phase 5 — Multi-tenant polish:** client onboarding flow, billing, alerts, exportable client reports, per-account quota dashboards.
166	
167	---
168	
169	## 10. Key Risks
170	
171	1. **API approvals slip the whole timeline** (see §3) — mitigate: start Day 1, keep read-only demo working on own accounts, over-prepare the screencast/onboarding flow.
172	2. **Rate limits** across three different models (BUC points / ops-day / RPM) — mitigate: centralized pacing, cache insights, batch mutations.
173	3. **Automation acting on noisy data** → wasted spend / client trust loss — mitigate: significance floors, cooldowns, dry-run, kill-switch, audit log.
174	4. **Overspend from platform delivery quirks** (2x/30.4x) — mitigate: hard caps + auto-pause projection.
175	5. **Breaking API version changes** (e.g., Google v23.x cadence) — mitigate: version-pinned clients, contract tests.
176	6. **Token/credential security** — encrypted vault, least-scope OAuth, rotation.
177	7. **Multi-platform data normalization** (differing attribution windows) — document and label; don't silently merge.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## 11. Compliance
182	
183	- **Meta Platform Terms & Developer Policies** govern all ad-data use. **Advertising data must NOT be combined with third-party/internal PII in a way that identifies an end user**, and must not be used for targeting/profiling outside the stated product functions. Business Verification + App Review enforce this.
184	- **Automated-rules compliance:** support auto-pausing ads that go "Rejected/Limited"; flag sensitive verticals (health, politics, finance) which have extra restrictions.
185	- **Data handling / PII:** store OAuth tokens encrypted; minimize PII; per-platform data-retention policy; GDPR/consent for any audience data; per-org data isolation (multi-tenant); full audit log of every mutation.
186	- **TikTok:** passes a data-security compliance audit; respect content/visibility rules.
187	- **Google:** Required Minimum Functionality + policy compliance for Standard access.
188	
189	Sources: [Meta platform terms/PII](https://www.adamigo.ai/blog/meta-conversion-data-compliance-best-practices), [Meta GDPR](https://www.adamigo.ai/blog/meta-ads-and-gdpr-compliance-guide), [Meta ad guidelines](https://adsuploader.com/blog/meta-ad-guidelines).
190	
191	---
192	
193	### Headline takeaway
194	The engineering is tractable and largely a normalization + scheduling problem; **the schedule is owned by external API approvals.** Kick off Meta business verification/app review, Google dev-token, and TikTok app review on Day 1 and build read-only against your own accounts while they clear.

## Sitewave (Marketing Agency) — Phase 1 (2026-08-10)

A productized web-design agency shipped as a Nxeon admin add-on module. **"Sitewave" is a placeholder
brand** (name, palette indigo `#4F46E5` + coral `#FB7185` + ink `#0B1020`, tagline "Websites that win you
customers.", placeholder demo domain `agency.revsports.ca` — stored as config in `lib/agency/config.ts`,
**not** resolved via DNS). Built on branch `feature/agency-sitewave-phase1`.

**The Phase 1 loop.** Add a *prospect* (a target business — manual or CSV, **no scraping**), assign a
*vertical*, then **Generate demo** → the generator writes a structured **Site IR** (JSON: hero copy,
services, about, CTA, an inspired-by palette) constrained to the vertical's section schema, and a
**deterministic renderer** turns the IR into a self-contained static HTML page. **Preview** it in a new tab.
**Deploy to subdomain** is a Phase-1 **stub** (records the intended `slug.agency.revsports.ca` host, marks
the demo `DEPLOYED_STUB` — no nginx/DNS/filesystem write). **Send to outreach** creates/links a Cold Email
`Business` + `Contact` from the prospect (reuses the existing coldemail models) but **sends nothing**.

**Generation (`lib/agency/generate.ts`).** Calls Claude via the platform `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
(`lib/anthropic.ts` `askClaude`, model `claude-opus-4-8`) to emit the Site IR as JSON. **Degrades
gracefully** exactly like `lib/marketing/draft-gen.ts`: with no key (or on any API/JSON error) it falls
back to a deterministic per-vertical template fill, so a demo is **always** produced. All output is coerced
through `coerceSiteIR` (`lib/agency/schema.ts`) which never throws — every field is defaulted, palette hex
validated, service/testimonial counts clamped.

**Legal guardrails baked into the renderer (`lib/agency/render.ts`).** Per architecture §11 (the biggest
risk), every rendered demo — LLM or fallback — carries: the business **name in plain type only** (no
re-hosted logo, ever), an **inspired-by palette** (never the business's exact brand), a visible
**"Independent concept — not affiliated with {business}"** disclaimer in both the top banner and the footer,
and `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`. All IR-derived text is HTML-escaped; the renderer is
pure + deterministic (no clock, no randomness, no network). It self-asserts the guardrails and
`generateDemo` **refuses to persist** a demo that fails the assertion. The preview route also sends
`X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.

**Schema additions (additive, all `Agency*`-prefixed — never touch VPS/hosting/coldemail models).**
`AgencyVertical` (slug, name, description), `AgencyTemplate` (verticalId, name, JSON `structure` /
section-schema), `AgencyProspect` (businessName, vertical, contactEmail?, currentSiteUrl?, pastedSiteText,
notes, `status` enum `PROSPECT|GENERATED|SENT|WON|LOST`, outreachBusinessId?), `AgencyDemoSite` (prospectId,
templateId?, `siteIR` Json, renderedHtml, slug, `status` enum `DRAFT|GENERATED|DEPLOYED_STUB`, `noindex`
default true, intendedHost?, deployedAt?), and `AgencyGenerationLog` (demoId, mode `llm|fallback`, model,
ok, message). Indexed on slug/status/vertical/createdAt/foreign keys. **Requires a migration before use —
this branch does NOT run `prisma db push`.**

**Starter template library (`lib/agency/templates.ts` + `prisma/seed-agency.ts`).** Five seeded verticals —
dentist, restaurant, gym, law firm, salon — each with a section schema (hero, services, about, testimonials,
contact) and deterministic fallback content. `templates.ts` is the single source of truth shared by the seed
and the generator's fallback, so the DB library and the no-API path stay in lockstep. Seed manually:
`NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed-agency.ts`.

**Admin surface** (new top-level **Agency** nav section, entry "Sitewave", icon `globe`; all routes map to
area `platform` = ADMIN-only): `/admin/agency` (overview — counts + prospects-by-status + LLM-availability
banner), `/admin/agency/verticals` (manage verticals + templates), `/admin/agency/prospects` (CRUD + CSV
paste + Generate demo + Send to outreach), `/admin/agency/demos` (list + preview + deploy-stub). Preview
serve route: `app/api/agency/demo/[id]/preview` (staff-gated, returns stored HTML with noindex headers).
Server actions live in `lib/actions-agency.ts` — **every export re-checks `requireArea("platform")`**.

**Phase 2 (documented, not built).** Real subdomain provisioning (reuse the shared-hosting name-based nginx
vhost + certbot SNI sweep + Namecheap wildcard DNS), live scrape/brand-extract → BrandProfile, a QA gate +
human-approve queue, a worker job/state-machine, and the `demo.ready` webhook to the Cold Email Engine with
open/click/claim tracking. See `scratchpad/projects/agency/architecture.md` + `board.json`.

**Guardrails honoured:** no real scraping, no outreach sending, no live provisioning, no `prisma db push`,
no `.env` edit, no deploy, not committed to main. `npx prisma generate` + `npm run build` both clean; the

## Adloop (Ads Autopilot) — Phase 1 (2026-08-10)

A cross-platform paid-ads management add-on shipped as a Nxeon admin module. **"Adloop" is a placeholder
brand** (name, palette emerald `#10B981` + amber `#F59E0B` + slate-900 `#0F172A`, tagline "Your ads, on
autopilot.", placeholder domain `ads.revsports.ca` — stored as config in `lib/ads/config.ts`, **not**
resolved via DNS). Built on branch `feature/ads-adloop-phase1`.

### ⚠️ External API-approval prerequisites — the long pole for the whole product

**Phase 1 is a SCAFFOLD. There are no live calls to Meta / TikTok / Google Ads, no real OAuth, and no ad
spend** — because programmatic ad management is gated on platform approvals that take **weeks of calendar
time** (architecture §3). Nothing beyond a self-account demo works until these clear, so they must be started
Day 1, in parallel:

- **Meta Marketing API** — every new app starts on Standard/Limited access (own accounts only); **Advanced/
  Full access** is required to manage third-party clients and needs **App Review + Business Verification + a
  screencast per permission + a working client-onboarding flow + a public privacy policy**. Business
  Verification a few business days; App Review commonly **1–3+ weeks**.
- **Google Ads API** — a developer token tied to a **Manager (MCC) account**, OAuth 2.0 per client, a Google
  Cloud project. Basic access **~5 business-day** review; Standard **~10 business-day** review. Token
  approval typically **5–14 business days** (a 2026-07-07 brand-verification pilot can shortcut it).
- **TikTok Marketing API v1.3** — dev registration → **Business Center onboarding** → sandbox→production app
  review → business verification → data-security audit. Basic **~3–7 business days**; advanced/high-volume
  **1–3 weeks**, quota increases case-by-case with no self-serve path and no published SLA.

The connectors in `lib/ads/connectors/` are therefore **stubs**: `MetaConnector` / `TikTokConnector` /
`GoogleConnector` all extend `StubConnector`, and every method (`listAccounts`, `listCampaigns`,
`fetchInsights`) resolves to a typed `{ ok: false, reason: "pending_approval" }` result with **no network
call**. `getConnector(platform)` is the pluggable registry seam — when a platform's access clears, swap its
entry for a real implementation and nothing else changes, because everything speaks the `AdsConnector`
interface (`lib/ads/types.ts`). Each `/admin/ads` page carries the banner **"Live ad-platform sync pending
API approval (Meta/TikTok/Google)"** and the Accounts tab lists the full per-platform approval checklist.

### The data layer (`lib/ads/*`)

- `types.ts` — the normalized, platform-agnostic contract: `InsightCounters`, `DerivedMetrics`, the rule
  `RuleCondition`/`RuleThen` shapes, and the `AdsConnector` interface. Note the **deliberate absence** of any
  live `applyAction` — Phase 1 rules are dry-run only.
- `metrics.ts` — pure metric derivation. `deriveMetrics` computes ctr/cpc/cpm/cpa/cvr, guarding every
  divide-by-zero to `null` (never NaN). Revenue/ROAS are omitted on purpose — the stub insight set only
  carries impressions/clicks/spend/conversions, so the dashboard shows only what stub data can honestly
  provide.
- `rules-engine.ts` — the **pure, testable DRY-RUN evaluator**. `evaluateRule(whenJson, thenJson, rows)`
  coerces malformed JSON (never throws), applies a significance floor (`minImpressions`), computes the
